headword: {公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}

definitions.explanation: The wife of a duke, or a woman who holds the rank of duke in her own right. The highest female title in the European peerage system below royalty.

examples.japanese: {公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
{公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{慈善活動|じぜんかつどう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: The duchess is known for her charitable activities.

examples.japanese: ⟦{小説|しょうせつ}→小説：01434_shousetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{主人公|しゅじんこう}→主人公：11404_shujinkou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{若|わか}い{公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、{社交界|しゃこうかい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{陰謀|いんぼう}→陰謀：10887_inbou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれて→巻き込む：05753_makikomu⟧いく。
examples.english: The novel's protagonist is a young duchess who becomes entangled in the intrigues of high society.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{公爵|こうしゃく}→公爵：17797_koushaku⟧ (duke) and ⟦{夫人|ふじん}→夫人：03597_fujin⟧ (wife, lady). This title belongs to the European peerage system and is encountered primarily in historical contexts, novels, and news about European aristocracy. Japan had its own ⟦{公爵|こうしゃく}→公爵：17797_koushaku⟧ rank in the {華族|かぞく} (nobility) system from 1884 to 1947.
